question: A federal department extended my access request because it has to consult another organization. What should the extension notice tell me?
generated_answer:
The extension notice should tell you the following:

- The reason for the extension (consultation with another organization)
- The new deadline for responding to your request
- Whether the extension will result in any additional fees
- Any other relevant details, such as which organization is being consulted and why

Example:

Dear [Your Name],

We are writing to inform you that your access request has been extended due to a requirement to consult with another organization.

Reason for extension: Consultation with [Organization Name] regarding shared information.

New deadline: [New Deadline]

Please note that this extension may result in additional fees. You will be notified if this is the case.

If you have any questions or concerns, please contact us at [Contact Information].

Thank you for your patience.

Best regards,
[Department Name]

This notice provides you with the necessary information to understand the reason for the extension and what to expect next. It also allows you to plan accordingly and, if necessary, prepare for any additional costs or actions. If you have any questions or concerns, don't hesitate to reach out to the department for clarification.
